      "category": "K1",
      "question": "What entry point and usage example will let the requester apply the helpers to real exports?",
      "changes": "The public export, documentation and consumer-facing verification.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks the package and existing consumers; absent further evidence, expose the record helper alongside squash from src/text.js and document a small CommonJS example.",
      "blocks": "The final consumer-facing usage check; nothing else if the default proceeds."

      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What were the old trim helper's name and record contract, including field selection, output shape and mutation?",
      "changes": "The new helper's name, inputs, output and compatibility tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first searches available repository history, documentation and consumers; if unavailable, provisionally use squashRecord, return a new object containing squashed own enumerable string-keyed fields, and leave the input unchanged. Confidence is low because the old helper is absent from this snapshot.",
      "blocks": "Finalizing the record-helper contract until discovery or the recorded default settles it."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "How should the record helper handle nullish records, non-record inputs, invalid field values, and unusual keys?",
      "changes": "Input validation, error behavior and edge-case tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first looks for the old helper's contract and consumer expectations; absent evidence, reject nullish and non-record inputs with TypeError, apply squash to each selected value, and propagate its TypeError for invalid fields while preserving keys safely.",
      "blocks": "Finalizing invalid-input and record edge-case tests until discovery or the recorded default settles them."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "Which existing string transformations and non-nullish type errors must remain unchanged across the full input space?",
      "changes": "Compatibility requirements and regression tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first establishes behavior from src/text.js and existing tests; preserve trim followed by JavaScript whitespace-run collapse for every string, and retain TypeError for every non-string except null and undefined.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the recorded behavior supplies the compatibility baseline."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What does usual whitespace mean where it might differ from the current JavaScript string behavior?",
      "changes": "Whitespace boundary tests and the implementation's character set.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks the existing implementation and any project contract; preserve the exact current trim and regular-expression whitespace semantics, including their existing Unicode behavior. Confidence is high because S9 requires exact string compatibility.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: existing string behavior resolves the default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "Do record consumers rely on shared references, prototypes, inherited or symbol properties, or mutation of their input?",
      "changes": "Record traversal, ownership and tests for input and output state.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks the old helper and consumers; absent evidence, process own enumerable string-keyed fields into a fresh plain object without mutating the input, with no persistent or shared runtime state. This provisional default excludes inherited and symbol fields.",
      "blocks": "Finalizing record state and property-selection semantics until discovery or the recorded default settles them."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q7",
      "category": "K6",
      "question": "Which Node versions and dependency constraints apply to this package?",
      "changes": "Syntax, APIs and the verification environment.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks package metadata and the available runtime; use the existing dependency-free CommonJS and node:test setup, with no new dependency or asserted minimum Node version unless evidence establishes one.",
      "blocks": "A claimed compatibility range; nothing else if the default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K7",
      "question": "Where does the existing package expect related helpers to be exported and tested?",
      "changes": "Module placement and the public test boundary.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks package metadata and consumers; place the helper with squash in src/text.js and exercise its CommonJS export from the existing test suite.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the existing module provides a provisional seam."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "Which checks demonstrate the nullish and type rules, exact string compatibility, and record behavior at the public boundary?",
      "changes": "Regression cases and completion evidence.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first examines the existing node:test conventions and settles the record contract; extend test/text.test.js and run npm test, covering representative whitespace, valid and invalid values, record fields and non-mutation if that contract is retained.",
      "blocks": "Final verification until the record contract is settled."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "Is a delivery location beyond the source checkout needed for tomorrow's export trial?",
      "changes": "The delivery step and access required.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks repository delivery instructions and consumer entry points; absent a named deployed target, deliver the usable helper in the source checkout at final return, with no assumed release or external write.",
      "blocks": "A deployment claim; nothing else if the checkout default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "Is there an established workload or performance budget for processing a million records?",
      "changes": "Performance acceptance evidence and any optimization decision.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first checks project benchmarks and consumer constraints; absent a budget, favor straightforward linear per-field work and avoid speculative optimization, recording that no numeric throughput guarantee was supplied.",
      "blocks": "A numeric performance guarantee; nothing else if the default proceeds."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "Where is the authoritative Orchard doc-comment style guide and what does it require?",
      "changes": "Doc-comment formatting and review criteria.",
      "route": "research",
      "default": "Discovery first checks installed guidance and repository documents, then authorized team documentation or owners; if the guide cannot be found, use the existing concise doc-comment style provisionally, with low confidence and without claiming Orchard compliance.",
      "blocks": "Verifying Orchard style compliance until the guide is found; other work can proceed under the provisional default."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q13",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "Can the host invoke the named code-review and improve skills, and what inputs and completion evidence do they require?",
      "changes": "The required review and improvement steps and their evidence.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Discovery first resolves the host's installed skill instructions and invocation mechanism; use code-review for edge cases followed by improve on its findings. If either is unavailable, record the limitation rather than claiming it ran.",
      "blocks": "Completion of the specifically requested skill review or improvement if the corresponding skill cannot be invoked; implementation discovery can continue."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "S1 [fact]: Scope is the records-helper repository and its existing consumers. S2 [fact]: squash must return an empty string for null and undefined and retain TypeError for numbers and objects; other existing non-nullish type errors are preserved by default (Q4). S3 [fact/open question]: Add a whole-record squash operation modeled on the old trim helper; discovery must establish its old contract and field/state rules, with provisional defaults in Q2, Q3 and Q6 before finalizing the interface and tests. S4 [fact/assumption]: Make the public helper usable by the requester for real exports tomorrow; discovery checks the entry point and delivery instructions, with a source-checkout delivery default (Q1, Q10). In an isolated run the source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return; a deployed outcome exists only after release, and no deployed target is named. S5 [fact/open question]: Use an installed review skill for edge cases, with code-review accepted, then run improve on its findings; discovery must establish skill availability and invocation before those steps can be completed (Q13). S6 [fact]: Keep any regular expressions readable in one pass. S7 [fact/default]: Use the existing JavaScript whitespace semantics as the compatibility baseline (Q5). S8 [fact/open question]: Follow the Orchard doc-comment guide; discovery must locate its authoritative text to verify compliance, with local comment style as a provisional fallback (Q12). S9 [fact]: Preserve all current string behavior exactly. S10 [fact]: Add tests in the existing node:test style and verify the public boundary (Q9). S11 [fact/default]: Keep million-record use in mind without premature optimization; discovery checks for an existing budget, and no numeric threshold is assumed (Q11). Discovery leads, not verified facts: the old trim helper and its consumers, repository history and package documentation, the host's code-review and improve skill instructions, and any authorized Orchard team documentation, channels or owners. No private locator was supplied; sensitive locators belong only in an authorized private store, never KNOWLEDGE/. This is intake only: no implementation, server, release or external write is authorized by this exercise. The product is a noninteractive library, so actor identification, cross-session sharing, hidden views and interactive session lifetime do not apply; record ownership and mutation remain covered by Q6."
